newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY SUPPORTS ETHNIC HUNGARIANS IN ROMANIAN GOVERNMENT.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY SUPPORTS ETHNIC HUNGARIANS IN ROMANIAN GOVERNMENT.

text.p: Hungary on Tuesday said the presence of representatives of Romania's 1.6 million ethic Hungarians in the new Romanian government would ensure Romania's adherence to commitments on minority rights.
"We welcome the fact that there is a chance the (ethnic Hungarian representatives) will get into the government," Hungarian foreign ministry spokesman Gabor Szentivanyi told Reuters.

"Their presence would strengthen Romania's ability and willingness to meet the international legal requirements that the previous government took on with organisations such as the Council of Europe," he said.

Since Emil Constantinescu and his party the Democratic Convention (CDR) won presidential and parliamentary elections earlier this month negotiations have been under way on forming a government between the CDR, Social Democrats and the Hungarian Democratic Union of Romania (UDMR).

On Tuesday Hungarian press reports, citing leaked information from the current negotations on forming a government, said the UDMR had been offered the posts of minister of tourism and minister without portfolio.
Szentivanyi said his government looked forward to seeing two ministerial posts going to the UDMR.
"We count on their presence as reflected in their electoral position," he said. "Having gained 7 percent of the vote... then this would mean two seats."
"It would be unique in the region that a political movement representing an ethnic minority could attain ministerial posts," he added.
When Romania joined the Council of Europe in 1993 it signed a protocol to protect the rights of ethnic minorities within its borders.

Hungary and Romania signed a basic treaty of friendship in September aimed at ending old quarrels by settling the status of Romania's 1.6 million ethnic Hungarians and guaranteeing Romania's western borders.
Hungary made no secret during the Romanian elections of its preference for Constantinescu and the CDR over the incumbent President Ion Iliescu.
Hungary saw the CDR as more supportive than Iliescu of the basic treaty while ethnic Hungarians in Romania thought Iliescu's party was pitting them against majority Romanians for political purposes.
Constantinescu is to be sworn in on Friday.
